# wlcs tests expected to fail in the phase tier, one gtest name per line (`Suite.test` or
# `Suite/Param.test/N`), each followed by `# <id>`; the ids are the rows below.
# dev/wlcs/run.sh --phase excludes them with --gtest_filter=-... (A6): never run and ignored,
# because each wlcs timeout costs 10 s. Regenerated by lane P0-wlcs against casement itself
# (wlcs-casement drives casement-testkit's Fixture: the real State on the headless backend; the
# earlier list was for a smithay stand-in). The whole suite (1225 tests run, 1291 gtest lines listed),
# sharded 12 ways in jails, after P0-layer-geom: 829 pass, 65 fail (listed here), 331 skip (wl_shell
# and zxdg_shell_v6 are not served, wlcs' own xfail self-tests). Before it: 596 pass, 298 fail. The
# list may only shrink. `CopyCutPaste.given_source_has_offered_when_sink_gets_focus_it_sees_offer`
# failed once in a 12-way shard run and passes alone (it has no roundtrip before its teardown): it is
# timing, not listed.
#
# Shim policies that decide what counts as a failure (wlcs-casement/src/host.rs):
#   - A37 (casement::relax, `testing` only): a buffer attached before the first ack is taken as the
#     ack and maps the window, as the compositors wlcs was written for do.
#   - a window that maps is activated with a valid token, because wlcs takes a newly mapped window
#     to be the active one and casement keys no window nobody asked for (A7).
#   - touch coordinates are whole pixels: wlcs' header says wl_fixed_t but its helpers (pinned SHA
#     and upstream main) pass plain ints.
#   - `position_window_absolute` on a layer surface pins it (`Event::LayerPlaced`): its anchors would
#     not let wlcs' layer-layer tests put two surfaces side by side.
#
# W1 (layer-shell) and W2 (xdg window geometry) were fixed by P0-layer-geom and have no entries left;
#     see FINDINGS.md "P0-layer-geom". The ids stay unused so the other rows keep their names.
# W3: xdg_wm_base error tests. smithay raises no error for get_xdg_surface on a surface that has a role
#     or a buffer (smithay fork patch needed), and attaching_buffer_to_unconfigured is the very rule the
#     A37 relaxation switches off for wlcs.
# W4: xdg_toplevel.wm_capabilities is expected after a roundtrip with no commit. The protocol sends it
#     with the first configure, which follows the first commit (xdg-shell.xml: once before the first
#     xdg_surface.configure): a wlcs-side expectation, not a casement bug.
# W5: FIXED by P0-output-enter (wl_surface.enter and leave for wl_output); no entry remains.
# W7: subsurface tests on an xdg parent: input stacking ignores place_above/place_below, and sync/desync
#     commit caching expectations differ (subsurfaces.cpp). Not diagnosed further.
# W8: xdg popup tests (grab, done order, keyboard focus, reposition, reactive parent move), the
#     layer-surface popups among them (the same four grab tests on `LayerShellPopup`). `xdg_popup.grab`
#     is refused: wlcs passes the client's latest serial of any event (a button release, a key) and the
#     seat's SerialBook proves presses only, so the popup is dismissed at once; with the proof bypassed
#     `grabbed_popup_gets_keyboard_focus` passes, and on layers
#     `grabbed_popups_get_done_events_in_correct_order` too. `popup_gives_up_pointer_focus_when_gone`
#     and `grabbed_popup_gets_done_event_when_new_toplevel_created` fail for another reason, not found.
#     The rest (reposition, reactive move, zero-size anchor rect) are not diagnosed; P0-H2 popups.
# W9: remaining pointer/touch input-region combinations. Not diagnosed further.
# W10: interactive move and resize tests: the pointer is not on the window when the test starts
#     (window_under_cursor is null). Not diagnosed further.
# W12: pointer constraints on reselection, primary selection, copy-cut-paste, text-input v3 with
#     input-method v2, decoration configure, viewporter and fractional-scale error checks: outside the
#     subset, not diagnosed.
# W13: a toplevel remapped after a null-buffer commit: casement waits for a new initial configure and
#     ack, wlcs re-attaches a buffer straight away (every builder of the `*_unmapped_and_remapped`
#     input-region tests: /4 and /5 were W13 already, /6 and /7 were tagged W2).
